verdict.rationale: ImageMagick's own docs list conversion across 200+ formats, naming PNG, JPEG, WebP and HEIC, and show a -quality flag for WebP compression and a -resize flag for size control, so the core of the story is delivered. SVG is not named in the first-party format list; it appears only in a community security warning that implies SVG is processed. Compression control is shown only through a single -quality example. missing for 10: first-party evidence of SVG conversion, documented compression controls beyond the -quality example (e.g. PNG compression level, lossless options, HEIC quality settings), independent hands-on corroboration of quality/compression tuning.

support.subject: As a power user, common image formats (PNG, JPEG, WebP, HEIC, SVG) convert with control over quality, size, and compression

citations.quote: Convert rapidly between 200+ standard formats (PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, TIFF).
# Convert PNG to WebP with compression $ magick input.png -quality 85 output.webp
# Resize image maintaining aspect ratio $ magick input.jpg -resize 800x600^ output.jpg
Transform: resize, rotate, deskew, crop, flip or trim an image.
